_doc: Source of truth for the recorded crew voices. Run tools/voice/generate.py after editing. `text` must match the game's subtitle text exactly (that is how World.callout lines find their clip). `roles` makes one clip per role (id__role), `vars` expands {key} in id/text (one clip per value, {i} = 1-based index), `say` overrides what is spoken, `rate` overrides words per minute, `urgent` speaks faster.

briefing.speaker: Intelligence Officer
briefing._doc: Mission briefings, one clip per paragraph (brief_<mission>_<n>), read in the briefing room: played clean by src/audio/BriefingVoice.ts, not through the radio chain. Generated from src/game/Missions.ts by tools/voice/briefings.mjs.

clock._doc: Short clips 'nine o'clock low!' for every hour x high/level/low, per role. Lines like 'Fighters, nine o'clock low!' play as prefix clip + clock clip (+ suffix clip).

lines.text: They're dropping their belly tanks — here they come!
Number {n} engine is hit! Feathering number {n}!
We can't hold formation. We're falling behind — keep those guns hot!
{name} is falling out of formation!
{who}! Somebody get him some help!

Lt. Frank Doyle is hit up front in the cockpit
Lt. Eli Stern is hit at the nav table

lines.text: Rockets! They're firing rockets into the formation!
Fire in number {n} engine!
Extinguisher's in. Fire's out on number {n}.
Extinguisher didn't take! Number {n} is still burning!
Fighters,
Bandit coming in,
Here he comes,
Fw one-ninety,
Get him!
That's five! You're an ace, gunner — drinks are on me tonight!
Got him! He's going down!
You got him! Nice shooting!
He's smoking — he's finished!
Scratch one Messerschmitt!
Scratch one Focke-Wulf!
{name} is going down! Count the chutes!
We've had it! Bail out! Bail out!
Gunner's hit! Stay on that gun if you can!
Pilot to crew: we're at altitude. Test fire your guns, and keep your eyes open.
Blue flight, form up on the bombers. Keep your eyes peeled for bandits.
Bandits,
More bandits,
Flak ahead. Initial point in two minutes — here it comes.
Bombs away! Let's get out of here!
Little friends at six o'clock high! The Mustangs are here!
Pilot to crew, oxygen check. Sound off.
Tail gunner, oxygen okay.
Navigator to pilot: on course, two-seven minutes to the IP.
Ball turret. Nothing below but cloud. Guns are clear.
Radio to pilot: group says keep it tight, fighters reported ahead.
Engineer to pilot: number three's running a little hot. Watching it.
Bombardier here. Keep your eyes open, they like to come out of the sun.
Stay off the interphone unless you see fighters. Keep scanning.
Blue flight, check your fuel. Weave over the big friends.
Little friends, little friends, thanks for the company.
Keep your heads on a swivel. They'll come out of the sun.
Blue Three, engine temps okay. Holding high cover.
Short bursts! You'll burn out that barrel!
Fighters coming up from the coast, nine o'clock low. Stay sharp.
More of them up ahead. Twelve o'clock — here they come.
More coming in on the left! Watch your nine!
Last bunch before the target. Make them count!
Bandits! Twelve o'clock high, a whole Staffel of them!
Fighters up high, coming out of the sun!
Fighters, three o'clock level! Coming in from the right!
We're through the flak. Here come the fighters again — watch the cripples.
Bandits twelve o'clock low, climbing for the bombers. Let's go get them.
Little friends, little friends, we have bandits at our six o'clock!
Fighters assembling behind us, six o'clock level. Lots of them.
Here comes the whole gaggle! Tail, they're all yours!
Another Staffel forming up astern!
Two fighters closing from six o'clock. They've spotted us.
Escort reports sixty seconds out. Hang on!
Here they come. Big gaggle at twelve o'clock — drop tanks and go!
More bandits! They're everywhere!
Here they come. Looks like the whole Luftwaffe is up today!
Bandits climbing out of the murk, twelve o'clock low. Blue flight, stay with me!
Fighters low on the water, six o'clock. They followed us out.
Bandits up high, going for the lead ships. Keep them off me till we're on the bomb run!
Pilot to crew, one more time. Fighters, twelve o'clock high, a lot of them!
Fighters coming in from six o'clock, get on the tail gun!
Ball turret, they're coming up from below!
Top turret, bandits high at twelve!
Left waist, bandits coming in at nine o'clock!
Right waist, fighters at three o'clock!
Bandits on the nose, twelve o'clock level!
Switch guns! They're coming in on the other side!
Good shooting, he's going down!
He's a flamer! Nice work!
I see a chute. He's out of it.
That's another one! Keep it up, gunner!
Watch your ammo, short bursts!
Ammo's getting low back there. Make 'em count!
Lead him more! Aim where he's going!
They're regrouping, here they come again!
Hang on, evasive action!
We're hit, we're hit!
Pilot to crew, damage check. Everybody okay back there?
She's still flying. Stay on those guns!
He's coming right at us! Keep firing!
They're going after the stragglers. Cover them!
Fighters forming up out there. Stand by, gunners.
Here comes the next wave, look sharp!
Round over. Nice work, gunners.
Keep scanning. They'll be back.
That's the last of them. We're going home, boys.
Blue two, break left!
Blue two, break right!
Bandit on your six!
Check six, Blue two! Check six!
Splash one!
Nice shooting, Blue two!
Blue three, splash one!
Bandits on the bombers! Go get 'em!
Blue two, you're trailing smoke!
Tally ho! Blue flight, drop tanks and engage!
Blue flight, regroup on me.
Sky's clear. Good work, Blue flight.
Thanks, little friends. That was close!
{who}! Somebody get him some help!

lines.text: Getting the feel of this gun now. Keep 'em coming!
I'm getting the hang of this. Send me another one!
Starting to see 'em before they see me.
Bomb bay doors coming open. Hold her steady…
Look at that… we hit it square!
Bombs on target! Look at it burn!
Smoke all the way to the river. The whole works is burning!
Secondary explosion! Something big just went up down there!
Hang on — evasive action!
Little friends coming in!
Little friends coming in! Red flight, sweep the bombers!
Pour it on, gunner! Give 'em everything!
Give 'em everything you've got, Blue two!
Steady... take your time. Lead him.
Steady, Blue two... line him up.
You're ready, gunner! Welcome to the crew of the Sky Queen.
This is a training flight, gunner. Nobody shoots back today. See that target drone? Put your sight on it.
Short bursts! Watch your tracers and walk them in.
Lead him! Aim where he's going to be, not where he is.
Use the ring sight for the long ones. Hold the right button.
Fighter on the other side! Somebody get on that gun!
Navigator here. Watch the radar plot — and Tab gives you the big picture.
Nice shooting. The ground crew fitted you something extra.
Here they come — three bandits. Show me what you've learned!
That's the last of them! Scratch one battle group — drinks are on me!
You got it just in time!
Nice shooting — that broke it up!
Rockets! Rockets incoming!
Jesus, that was close! She nearly took our tail off!
Turret knocked out! Keep at it!
Rocket pod went up like a firework!
Engine hit! She's dropping back!
Fighters dropping out of that thing's belly!
She's breaking up! That's the last of them!
Look at her go — she's breaking in two!
Hold still — I've patched you up. Back on that gun.
That one's an ace — kill markings all down the tail. Watch him!
That's the last of the destroyers! Nice work, boys.
Rocket barrage! Heavies standing off at a kilometre — they'll keep lobbing rockets into the box until we knock them down!
Launchers are down! That's the end of the rockets.
They're out of rockets — the heavies are heading home.
The yellow noses are breaking off — they've lost their leader!
That's the lot of them! They're breaking off!
He's reversing — scissors! Throttle back, make him fly out in front!
Head-on! Hold your fire till he's close, then break high!
Watch it, Blue two — his wingman is sliding in behind you!
He's spiralling down — don't follow him into the deck!
Focke-Wulf's zooming up for another pass. Keep your speed!
Thanks, little friend — he was all over us!
We owe you one, little friend. We're going to make it!
Bandits twelve o'clock low, climbing for the bombers. Get between them and the big friends!
Little friends, twin-engine bandits closing at our six — they've got rockets!
Another gaggle, nine o'clock level. Some of them are coming for us!
Heads up — 109s high at six, coming down on us! Break and engage!
Bandits on the bombers, twelve o'clock! Little friends, where are you?
Focke-Wulfs diving out of the sun — don't try to out-climb them!
Bandits going for the cripple! Blue two, get back there and cover her!
More of them coming in on our tail — we can't take another pass!
One last pass at the box, twelve o'clock. Let's finish this!
Big gaggle at twelve o'clock — drop tanks and go! Hit them before they reach the box!
Zerstörers at six o'clock, with rockets! Get them off us!
Jets! Twelve o'clock high, fast movers — go for them when they slow down!
Messerschmitts, high at five o'clock! Here they come — break!
Jets coming through! You won't out-run them — turn inside them!
Fighters on the bombers, twelve o'clock level!
They're sending another Gruppe down on us. Stay together!
They're on the straggler! Blue two, cover her, I'll take the box!
Jet coming up our tail! Somebody get him off us!
Last push — they're throwing everything at the box!
Blue Two, engaging your target!
Blue Two — no target in front of you, staying on your wing.
Blue Two, covering your six!
Blue Two, going to the bombers!
Blue Two, going after the bombers!
Blue Two, forming up on your wing.
Bandit on your tail — Blue Two is on him!
Blue Two — splash one!
Blue Two, I'm hit! I'm going down!
Blue Two, replacement aircraft joining on your wing.
Control to Blue flight: raid inbound, Junkers with fighter cover. Get between them and the airfield!
Control, second wave: bombers and Messerschmitts on the same heading. Hit the bombers first!
Control: this is the main raid — everything they've got. Don't let them through!
Control to Blue flight: raiders crossing the coast in the dark. Look for their exhaust flames and the searchlights.
Control: more of them coming in, with night fighters. The searchlights will find the bombers for you.
Control: the main stream is inbound. Every one you get is one less over the field!
Bombs on the airfield! Stop the rest of them!
He's dumped his bombs — he's turning for home!
Messerschmitts coming down on us — they're covering the bombers!
Searchlights have one coned! Get him while he's lit!
Blue Four, engaging your target!
Blue Four — no target in front of you, staying on your wing.
Blue Four, covering your six!
Blue Four, going to the bombers!
Blue Four, going after the bombers!
Blue Four, forming up on your wing.
Bandit on your tail — Blue Four is on him!
Blue Four — splash one!
Blue Four, I'm hit! I'm going down!
Blue Four, replacement aircraft joining on your wing.
That one bounced right off the armour plate!
Flak coming up — heavy guns below us. Hold steady.
Intelligence was right — that's {name}'s machine! Watch for his markings!
You got {name}! That's one Experte off the board!
Those markings again — it's the same Experte we tangled with before!
He's back — you can still see the patches where we shot him up!
That's the one who bailed out on us — he's flying again!
He's breaking off, trailing smoke — don't let him get away!
He got away. He'll be back — and he'll remember us.
He's bailed out — there's his chute! He'll fly again.
Somebody got the Experte! Scratch one ace!
That was the Experte! He got one of ours!
The Experte just got one of the Forts!
He's coming straight for us — he's got a score to settle!
He's going after the Mustangs — he wants the little friends!
He's going for the stragglers — the cripples are his meat!
He's lining up on the tail gun — watch six o'clock!
Sturmbock! Armoured Fw 190s closing to point-blank — hit him hard!
lines.say: Sturmbock! Armoured Focke-Wulfs closing to point-blank, hit him hard!

lines.text: He's coming head-on, twelve o'clock high — he never turns away first!
He's coming out of the sun — watch the glare!
Jet Experte! One pass and he's gone — be ready!
That Me 410 Experte is hanging back — he'll use the big gun!
lines.say: That M E four-ten Experte is hanging back, he will use the big gun!

lines.group: mission bookends: take-off and landing at Deenethorpe (src/game/Bookends.ts)

lines.text: Deenethorpe tower to Sky Queen: you are cleared for take-off. Good hunting.
lines.say: Deenthorpe tower to Sky Queen: you are cleared for take-off. Good hunting.

lines.text: Tail wheel locked… full power.
lines.say: Tail wheel locked... full power.

lines.text: Ninety… one-ten… she's flying! Gear up.
lines.say: Ninety... one ten... she's flying! Gear up!

lines.text: Pilot to crew: climbing through the overcast. We form up on top.
Pilot to crew: letting down through the overcast. We're nearly home.
Sky Queen, you are number one to land. Welcome home.
Wounded aboard — firing red flares!
Crash crew, stand by! Ambulances to the runway!
The gear won't come down — brace for a belly landing!
We're down! Everybody out — move!
Home in one piece. Nice work, everybody.

lines.group: Phase 5 night + weather fronts (RaidDefence.ts pathfinders / World.weatherFront)

lines.text: Control: pathfinder flares going down over the field! The bombers will aim on them — get under the flares and you'll see them.
Storm front dead ahead. Tighten it up — we're going right through it.
Blue flight, storm front dead ahead. Close it up and stay on my wing in the murk.
We're breaking out of the cloud — clear sky ahead. They'll see us coming now.
Blue flight, the cloud's breaking up. Clear sky ahead — keep your eyes open.
Me 410 hanging back out of range — he's carrying a fifty-millimetre cannon!
lines.say: M E four-ten hanging back out of range — he's carrying a fifty-millimetre cannon!

lines.text: Me 410 lining up with the big gun!
lines.say: M E four-ten lining up with the big gun!

lines.text: He's firing the big gun! Kill him before he reloads!
Got the Me 410 before he could fire!
lines.say: Got the M E four-ten before he could fire!

lines.text: Do 335 diving on us from high astern — he's as fast as a jet!
lines.say: Dornier three-thirty-five diving on us from high astern — he's as fast as a jet!

lines.text: Heinkels! A whole formation of bombers — get into them before they reach the target!
German bombers crossing ahead — a whole formation of Heinkels!
Control to Blue flight: a supply train is heading east for the tunnel. Stop that locomotive before it gets there!
Control: a truck convoy is on the road to the village. Shoot it up before it gets under cover!
Control: the Luftwaffe field to the north-east. Strafe the aircraft on the ground — and watch the flak!
Got the loco! She's blown her boiler!
The train made it into the tunnel. Too late, Blue flight.
Light flak coming up! Stay low and keep jinking!
Focke-Wulfs coming down on us! Watch your tail, Leader!
Blue Two, going down on your target!
Blue Two — got one on the ground!
Blue Leader, you are leaving the target area. Come back round.

lines.group: Phase 5 formation set pieces (SetPieces.ts / RandomEvents.ts straggler)

lines.text: Direct hit on the ship next to us! Her wing's folding up!
Debris coming through! Hang on!
She's rolling over… she's going into a flat spin. Get out, fellas — get out of there!
Chute! I see a chute!
I count {pair}…
That's all. Ten men on that ship… God help the rest of them.
That's all I see. Come on… come on… that's all of them.
That one-ninety's on fire — he's not pulling out! He's going to ram her!
He hit her! Oh God, they're locked together!
They're going down together… I don't see anybody getting out.
One chute! One man got out!
Got him before he hit her! That was too close!
She's hit in the bomb bay — she's burning! She's going to blow!
Wing section coming past the window — look out!
She's gone. The whole ship… just gone.
Crew, check in! Is anybody hurt back there?
Tail's okay. Just… shook up.
She's feathered two engines — she can't keep up! She's dropping out!
They're chewing us to pieces back here! For God's sake, somebody help us!
She's going down… we couldn't do a thing for her.
Big friends, hold your fire — Mustangs coming through!
Little friends! Right past the window — they're all over him!
They got him! God bless those little friends!
Well, that's one. First thing tomorrow I'm painting a bomb under the window.
I counted forty-one holes in her. Forty-one, and not one of them in us.
Emden on the first try. I said I would.
Told you. Nobody can find me down in that ball.
Nobody wants to, Shorty.
My hands didn't stop shaking till we crossed the English coast. Is that normal?
It's normal. Mine haven't stopped yet.
Get some sleep, all of you. One down. Twenty-four to go.
They came straight at the nose. All I could see was the propeller hub and the guns winking at me.
That top turret earned its keep today. Twin fifties, and somebody who knew what to do with them.
Lieutenant, you've been humming the same four bars since we landed.
It helps. Don't ask me why. It helps.
Two down. I'm keeping the tally in the back of my navigation log.
Fog's coming in. Maybe they'll stand us down tomorrow.
Maybe. Sleep while you can.
They came for the Lucky Lady's things an hour ago. Folded the blankets. Took the photographs off the wall.
Their tail gunner owed me two dollars. I'd give anything for him to walk in here and not pay it.
Sixty Fortresses. Six hundred men. I keep doing the arithmetic, and it keeps coming out the same.
From the ball I could see the chutes. I tried to count them. I couldn't keep up.
I lit a candle for them in the chapel. I didn't know what else to do.
Still got the rabbit's foot. I don't know if that makes me lucky, or them not.
We came home. Tomorrow we'll think about why. Tonight, try to sleep.
There he is. The Mustang that stayed with us all the way to Kiel. Sit down, sir. Dinner's on me.
lines.say: There he is. The Mustang that stayed with us all the way to Keel. Sit down, sir. Dinner's on me.

lines.text: For a month, Hawkeye. You said a month. The whole ship heard you on the interphone.
I know what I said. Worth every penny.
We couldn't see our own wingtips in that front. When the Germans came through the gaps, you were already there.
The first time anyone's gone all the way with us. It changes the arithmetic.
To the little friends.
To the little friends. May they never run short of fuel.
Same time tomorrow, sir? I'll bring my wallet.
Two hundred guns down there, and I still put the bombs right on the aiming point. I've never seen flak like it.
Merry Christmas, Ray. Five days late.
Every gun had its Saint Christopher today, and every one of us came home. I'm not saying it's the medals. I'm not saying it isn't.
On Christmas Eve I kept thinking about the Lucky Lady's boys. They'd have liked the snow.
Tomorrow is the last day of the year. Nineteen forty-four, gentlemen.
Next Christmas at home. Everybody say it.
Next Christmas at home.
I kissed that runway, and I'd do it again. The RAF boys think I've gone flak happy.
They took Frank to the hospital. The surgeon says he'll keep the leg.
I told you. I wasn't putting an old lady in the Channel on her thirteenth.
When the Spitfires showed up off the coast, I could have cried. Maybe I did.
Somebody write to Frank tonight. Tell him the old lady made it.
I'll write it. I'll make it long. He hates long letters.
Lights out. We fly home in the morning.
Leipzig and back, and not one of them got through to us. I said there was a steak in it, didn't I?
lines.say: Lipe-zig and back, and not one of them got through to us. I said there was a steak in it, didn't I?

lines.text: He's been saving his coupons for a week. Don't ask him where he found a steak in England.
Big Week, they're calling it. The whole Eighth went out today, all of us after the aircraft factories.
When that Fortress fell out of formation, I thought she was finished. Then you came down on the wolves.
Frank wrote from the hospital. He says the nurses are lovely and the food is a crime.
There's a rumour we're going back to Schweinfurt. Nobody say it out loud.
lines.say: There's a rumour we're going back to Shvine-foort. Nobody say it out loud.

lines.text: Eat your steak, sir. You earned it.
Schweinfurt. There, I said it. Somebody had to.
lines.say: Shvine-foort. There, I said it. Somebody had to.

lines.text: A hundred yards. I could see the rounds sparking off their windscreens, and they still didn't break.
I've got my piece of Frankfurt on my key ring. It came up through the floor and found my leg. I'm keeping it.
Sixty ships stayed behind the last time. Today we brought ours home. That's enough for me.
Nineteen missions. Six to go. I don't like saying the number out loud either.
Same socks tomorrow. Don't anybody say a word.
Long day tomorrow. Lights out in ten minutes.
Right on the aiming point. I've seen the photographs. The assembly hall is gone.
He's shown everybody the photographs. Twice. He showed the barman.
I waited nineteen missions for that target. I'm entitled.
Four minutes straight and level through that flak. I said it in September and I'll say it now. I do not like flak.
Noted, Sergeant.
Every Messerschmitt they don't build is one that won't be waiting for the next crew. Remember that.
Buy the man a drink. Even if he is insufferable.
I'll take it.
Two engines, all the way across Holland. I listened to every cylinder the whole way home.
Twenty-two missions, and she carried us home again.
When the Mustangs came over the horizon, Price started laughing and couldn't stop.
Wasn't laughing. Something in my eye.
The ground crew has been out there since we landed. In the rain, with lamps. They say she'll be ready by Wednesday.
Somebody take those boys a thermos of coffee. They've earned it more than we have.
I'll go. I owe them.
We all do.
Berlin. We went to Berlin and back, and the Mustangs never left us.
I saw a Fortress with a crown on her nose get a lot of extra cover today. Somebody told you, didn't they?
I painted that crown. I'm taking the credit for the whole escort.
They say the Luftwaffe lost more today than it can replace. You could feel it. They didn't press like they used to.
The ground crew put her back together in two days. She flew today with every man who wouldn't leave her.
I've stopped pretending I don't count the missions. We're close now.
To the little friends. Again.
And put it on my tab.
I rubbed out the pencil. It's in paint now. Twenty-five bombs under the window.
In paint. Now it counts.
I went out to her after we landed and put my hand on number three engine. Still warm. I said thank you.
I'm going to miss the ball. Don't tell anybody I said that.
I'm burning these socks. Out behind the hut, a proper funeral.
Twenty-five missions. I've worked it out a dozen ways, and it never adds up to why we came home and the others didn't.
I want to say something about the Lucky Lady's boys. And the new crews who never finished their first week.
We knew some of their names. Not all of them. We carry them home anyway.
Twenty-five missions and never a scratch. I think about that more than I should.
First thing, I'm going to stand in the middle of the cornfield and look at the sky. Just look at it.
The ranch will still be there. Cattle don't know there was a war.
Brooklyn. My mother's going to cook for three days, and I'm going to let her.
Boston. I'm singing at my sister's wedding, and this time I'll know all the words.
Philadelphia. A classroom full of kids who think arithmetic is boring. God bless every one of them.
San Antonio. I'm going to fix my father's truck, and nobody is going to shoot at me while I do it.
I'm going to sleep for a week. Then I'll think about it.
Kansas. Low and slow over the wheat, and nobody shooting.
It was an honour to fly with every one of you. Thank you.
lines.say: It was an honor to fly with every one of you. Thank you.

lines.text: Somebody wind up the gramophone.
Twenty-five. Let's go home.
Doc says {name} will be in the hospital a week or two. I'll take him his mail.
{name} is in the next bed over. He asked us to keep his place by the stove.
We'll go over and see him in the morning.
We'll go over and see them both in the morning.
How are you holding up, {nick}?
Doc put a few stitches in it. I'll be flying the next one.
Every ship in the group came home today. I counted them twice.
One ship didn't come back today. Ten men.
Two ships went down today. Twenty men.
{n} ships didn't come back today. I wrote down every name I knew.
They came for the bunks across the aisle an hour ago. Folded the blankets. Took the photographs down.
Nobody sleeps in those bunks tonight. Leave them be.
{ace} won't be back. I watched him go down.
{ace} got away from us again. He'll be back.
That was your shooting. Don't go looking for a parade. There was a man in that cockpit, too.
Intelligence says the Luftwaffe is running short of pilots. You can see it. The new ones break off early.
Intelligence says they're stronger than they were a month ago. More of them every time we go.
Then we fly a tighter formation.
Intelligence calls it even. They lose fighters, they build more. So do we.
Didn't get one today? Don't let it eat at you. Every burst you fired kept one of them off us.
You got one today. Some fellows fly ten missions and never see one fall.
The low squadron saw you knock them down, one after another. They're asking who was on that gun.
Five or more in one day. They're putting your name in for the Cross, and I'm telling everybody I know you.
You shoot like a man who's paying for his own shells.
The armourers say you nearly burned out a barrel. Short bursts. Let the gun cool between them.
lines.say: The armorers say you nearly burned out a barrel. Short bursts. Let the gun cool between them.

lines.text: You didn't get one? Doesn't matter. Every time one of them saw you coming, he broke off.
I watched you from the tail. You came down on them like a hawk on a chicken run.
Five or more, the way Dawson tells it. Somebody paint a row of crosses under that canopy.

lines.group: fighter bookends: P-51 take-off and landing at Boxted (src/game/FighterBookends.ts)

lines.text: Boxted tower to Blue flight: you are cleared for take-off. Good hunting.
Blue Four, rolling with you.
Blue flight, Big Friends at twelve o'clock low. Take station on the box.
Blue flight, initial for the break. Breaking left.
Blue flight, cleared to land. Welcome home.
Engine's gone — coming in dead-stick!
lines.say: Engine's gone! Coming in dead stick!

lines.text: Gear won't come down — I'm putting her down on her belly!
lines.say: Gear won't come down! I'm putting her down on her belly!

lines.text: Crash crew to the runway! Mustang coming in wheels up!
Blue Four is down. Nice flying today, Two.
Gentlemen, this is your first one. The group puts up eighteen ships against the U-boat yards at Emden. Bombing altitude twenty-five thousand feet.
You are left waist gunner aboard the Sky Queen, number two ship in the lead element. Expect single-engine fighters over the Frisian coast. They will come in fast and they will come in close.
Lead your target. A fighter crossing at three hundred miles an hour needs a lot of lead — watch your tracers and walk them in. Short bursts. Keep that barrel cool.

A word about your ship. The Sky Queen is brand new, and so is her crew. Captain Brenner flies her, Lieutenant Stern has promised to find Emden on the first try, and Sergeant Gallo has already painted a crown under the pilot's window. Twenty-five missions and you go home. This is number one.
The Luftwaffe has learned that the nose of a Fortress is its weak spot. Their fighters are making head-on passes at closing speeds of six hundred miles an hour.
You are flying the top turret today. Twin fifties, three hundred and sixty degrees of traverse. When they come in from twelve o'clock high you are the man who has to stop them.
Bremen is heavily defended. Expect repeated attacks before and after the target.

The Sky Queen came back from Emden with forty-one holes in her and not a scratch on her crew. Sergeant Reilly says the ball turret is the safest seat in the house, because the Germans cannot find him down there. Lieutenant Doyle says nobody else can either. Mission two. Keep it off the interphone once we cross the coast.

Gentlemen, the target is Schweinfurt. Half the ball bearings in Germany come out of five factories in one small town. Flatten them, and every tank, U-boat and fighter in the Reich will feel it. The Eighth is putting up nearly three hundred Fortresses, and the Luftwaffe knows we are coming.
lines.say: Gentlemen, the target is Shvine-foort. Half the ball bearings in Germany come out of five factories in one small town. Flatten them, and every tank, U-boat and fighter in the Reich will feel it. The Eighth is putting up nearly three hundred Fortresses, and the Luftwaffe knows we are coming.

lines.text: The escort turns back at Aachen. After that we are on our own for two hundred miles, and intelligence expects every fighter group in western Germany to be waiting: single-engine fighters head-on, twin-engine destroyers firing rockets from astern. They will hit us in relays, land, refuel and come up again.
lines.say: The escort turns back at Ahken. After that we are on our own for two hundred miles, and intelligence expects every fighter group in western Germany to be waiting: single-engine fighters head-on, twin-engine destroyers firing rockets from astern. They will hit us in relays, land, refuel and come up again.

lines.text: You are in the ball turret today. Keep it turning, keep calling them out, and watch the bellies of the low squadron. Nobody else can see what is coming up from below.

This is the Sky Queen's third mission. Lieutenant Doyle wants it on the record that he volunteered for a milk run and nobody offered him one. Fly tight. Today a tight formation is the only escort you will have.

Until now the bombers have gone into Germany alone the moment the escort ran short of fuel. As of today that changes. The Mustang can reach Kiel and come home again, and you are going all the way with them.
lines.say: Until now the bombers have gone into Germany alone the moment the escort ran short of fuel. As of today that changes. The Mustang can reach Keel and come home again, and you are going all the way with them.

lines.text: The weather is the worst we have flown in. A front lies across the North Sea from the Frisian Islands to Denmark: towering cloud, icing above eight thousand feet and lightning in the tops. We take off in clear air, and you will see it ahead long before we reach it. Once we are in, stay on your leader's wing in the murk. The German fighters will come at the bombers through the gaps.

The bomber crews are watching you today. The Sky Queen's tail gunner, Sergeant Dawson, has seen too many friends go down after the escort turned for home. He says that if a Mustang sticks with them all the way to Kiel, he will buy its pilot dinner for a month.
lines.say: The bomber crews are watching you today. The Sky Queen's tail gunner, Sergeant Dawson, has seen too many friends go down after the escort turned for home. He says that if a Mustang sticks with them all the way to Keel, he will buy its pilot dinner for a month.

lines.text: Mouse aim flies the aeroplane where you look. Keep your speed up, do not chase them into the cloud, and stay with the big friends.

The I.G. Farben works at Ludwigshafen is ringed by more than two hundred heavy flak guns. There is nothing you can do about flak but pray — and keep the fighters off us. The forecast has the overcast breaking up short of the target, so the gunners down there will have a clear view of us.
lines.say: The I G Farben works at Lood-vigs-hahfen is ringed by more than two hundred heavy flak guns. There is nothing you can do about flak but pray — and keep the fighters off us. The forecast has the overcast breaking up short of the target, so the gunners down there will have a clear view of us.

lines.text: You are right waist gunner. Fighters will hit us on the way in, then pull off when we reach the flak belt. Once bombs are away, they will be back for the cripples.
Stay at your gun through the bomb run. Do not get out of position.

Since Schweinfurt the bunks across the aisle have changed names twice. The Lucky Lady never came back from that one, and her crew had been with the Sky Queen since training. Sergeant Mendez has blessed every gun aboard with a Saint Christopher medal. Lieutenant Kessler wants only one thing for Christmas: the aiming point.
lines.say: Since Shvine-foort the bunks across the aisle have changed names twice. The Lucky Lady never came back from that one, and her crew had been with the Sky Queen since training. Sergeant Mendez has blessed every gun aboard with a Saint Christopher medal. Lieutenant Kessler wants only one thing for Christmas: the aiming point.

lines.text: Frankfurt is burning behind us, and so is the Sky Queen. Flak over the target knocked out two engines and put Lieutenant Doyle on the floor of the cockpit with a piece of steel in his leg. The group could not wait for us. We are alone, low on fuel, and the sun is going down.

Lieutenant Stern has plotted the shortest line home: across Belgium and out over the Channel past Dunkirk. Every fighter field in Flanders sits under that line. Sergeant Gallo is calling Air-Sea Rescue every five minutes, and the crew has thrown out everything that is not bolted down, except the guns.

The Germans love a straggler at dusk. They will come out of the dark side of the sky, low over the water where you cannot see them against the sea. Watch the east, and use every gun position, one through five.

Fighter Command has promised an escort off the coast. Hold out until it gets here. Captain Brenner says this is the Sky Queen's thirteenth mission, and he is not putting an old lady in the Channel on her thirteenth.
Big Week. The whole Eighth Air Force is going after the German aircraft industry, and this time the bombers will not go alone.

You are flying a P-51D Mustang on close escort for a box of twelve Fortresses. First the Focke-Wulfs and Zerstörers will go for the bombers — intercept them before they reach the box. Then expect a fighter sweep of 109s hunting the escort, flying in pairs: watch for the wingman. And if a Fortress falls out of formation, the wolves will go for her. Do not let them.
lines.say: You are flying a P fifty-one D Mustang on close escort for a box of twelve Fortresses. First the Focke-Wulfs and Zerstörers will go for the bombers — intercept them before they reach the box. Then expect a fighter sweep of 109s hunting the escort, flying in pairs: watch for the wingman. And if a Fortress falls out of formation, the wolves will go for her. Do not let them.

lines.text: Mouse aim flies the aircraft toward where you look. W and S for throttle, V for cockpit or chase view, T padlocks the nearest bandit. Your six fifties are harmonised at two hundred and fifty metres — get in close.

Some of you met the Sky Queen's crew in the pub at Oundle after Kiel. Their tail gunner, Sergeant Dawson, is still paying for dinners for the Mustang pilots who went all the way with them. He says there is a steak in it for anyone who sees them home from Leipzig.
lines.say: Some of you met the Sky Queen's crew in the pub at Oundle after Keel. Their tail gunner, Sergeant Dawson, is still paying for dinners for the Mustang pilots who went all the way with them. He says there is a steak in it for anyone who sees them home from Leipzig.

lines.text: Intelligence reports a new kind of German unit: the Sturmgruppe. Heavily armoured Fw 190 A-8s that close to point-blank range from astern, in line abreast, and do not break off.
lines.say: Intelligence reports a new kind of German unit: the Shtoorm-groopa. Heavily armoured Focke-Wulf one-ninety A eights that close to point-blank range from astern, in line abreast, and do not break off.

lines.text: You are the tail gunner. They will be coming straight at you. Open fire early and keep firing — armour glass in their windscreens will stop a lot of what you throw at them.

The Sky Queen is one of the senior ships in the group now, with eighteen missions behind her. Lieutenant Doyle is back from hospital with a piece of Frankfurt flak on his key ring, and nobody aboard will say the word Schweinfurt out loud. The last time we went there, sixty Fortresses stayed behind. Not today.
lines.say: The Sky Queen is one of the senior ships in the group now, with eighteen missions behind her. Lieutenant Doyle is back from hospital with a piece of Frankfurt flak on his key ring, and nobody aboard will say the word Shvine-foort out loud. The last time we went there, sixty Fortresses stayed behind. Not today.

lines.text: This is the last day of Big Week, and the target is the one the group paid for so dearly in August: the Messerschmitt works at Regensburg. Every Bf 109 that has come at you this week was built under that roof. Today we take the roof off.
lines.say: This is the last day of Big Week, and the target is the one the group paid for so dearly in August: the Messerschmitt works at Ray-gens-boorg. Every Messerschmitt one-oh-nine that has come at you this week was built under that roof. Today we take the roof off.

lines.text: The plant is ringed by heavy guns, and they will fire a box barrage straight up the bomb run. From the initial point to bombs away is four minutes of straight and level flying. No evasive action. The Sky Queen holds her place in the formation and takes it.

Lieutenant Kessler has waited nineteen missions for a target like this. He spent the night with the target photographs and says he could find the assembly hall in his sleep. Your job is to keep the fighters off him until he does. You have the top turret, and they will come for the lead ships from above.
Sergeant Mendez has asked me to remind everyone that he does not like flak, and that he has been saying so since September. Noted, Sergeant. Bombs away is what this whole war is about. Make it count.
Flak over Berlin knocked out two of our engines. We cannot hold formation and the group is pulling away from us. A lone Fortress is exactly what the Jagdflieger are looking for.
lines.say: Flak over Berlin knocked out two of our engines. We cannot hold formation and the group is pulling away from us. A lone Fortress is exactly what the Yahkt-fleeger are looking for.

lines.text: Every gun aboard is manned. Switch positions as they come in — one through five. P-51s are on the way to pick us up, but we have to hold out until they get here.
lines.say: Every gun aboard is manned. Switch positions as they come in — one through five. P fifty-ones are on the way to pick us up, but we have to hold out until they get here.

lines.text: Sergeant Gallo is calling every station that will listen. Lieutenant Stern has us on a heading for the coast, and Captain Brenner has told the crew that the Sky Queen did not carry them through twenty-one missions to let them down now. Hold on.
This is the big one. The Luftwaffe is throwing everything it has left at the bomber stream over Berlin.

You lead the escort for our box. Rocket-armed Zerstörers will try to break up the formation, then the 109s and the new jets will come for the escort. The Me 262 is faster than anything we have — do not chase it, turn inside it and catch it when it comes back round. Bf 110s carry a rear gunner: come at them from below.
Over the target a crippled Fortress will need you. Pick your targets, protect the bombers, and keep your speed up.

The Sky Queen made it home on two engines two days ago. The ground crew worked on her all night, and she is flying today with the men who would not leave her. When you see a Fortress with a crown painted under the cockpit, give her a little extra cover. She has three missions to go.

Gentlemen, this is a maximum effort. Big Week broke the back of the German fighter arm; today we finish the job. More than nine hundred heavy bombers are going after the aircraft plants at Oschersleben, Bernburg and Stettin, and the Luftwaffe will throw everything it has left at us.
lines.say: Gentlemen, this is a maximum effort. Big Week broke the back of the German fighter arm; today we finish the job. More than nine hundred heavy bombers are going after the aircraft plants at Oshers-layben, Bernburg and Stettin, and the Luftwaffe will throw everything it has left at us.

lines.text: There are Mustangs all the way to the target now, so the Germans hit the bomber stream before the escort can join. Expect a heavy attack on the way in, flak over the target, and a last fight before the little friends arrive. Hold on until they get there.

For the Sky Queen this is mission twenty-five. When she lands, her crew goes home. Lieutenant Doyle is back in the right-hand seat with a new limp and the same old jokes, and Sergeant Gallo has already painted the twenty-fifth bomb under the cockpit window. In pencil, he says, so it does not count as bad luck.

You are back on the left waist gun, where you started at Emden. Think of the crews who are not here today: the Lucky Lady over Schweinfurt, and the new boys who never finished their first week. Fly this one for them. Then come home, all of you.
lines.say: You are back on the left waist gun, where you started at Emden. Think of the crews who are not here today: the Lucky Lady over Shvine-foort, and the new boys who never finished their first week. Fly this one for them. Then come home, all of you.
